definitions.explanation: An area of grass, trees, or other vegetation, especially one set aside for recreational use or environmental preservation in an urban setting.

examples.japanese: {都市|とし}には{緑地|りょくち}が{必要|ひつよう}だ。
{駅前|えきまえ}に{新|あたら}しい{緑地|りょくち}が{整備|せいび}された。
examples.english: A new green area was developed in front of the station.

examples.japanese: マンションの{周|まわ}りに{緑地|りょくち}が{広|ひろ}がっているので、{子|こ}どもを{安心|あんしん}して{遊|あそ}ばせられる。
examples.english: There's green space spread around the apartment building, so I can let my children play there without worry.

notes:
A compound of {緑|りょく} (green) and {地|ち} (ground; land). Used in urban planning and environmental contexts to describe areas of vegetation preserved or created within developed areas. Japan's {都市|とし}{計画法|けいかくほう} (City Planning Act) defines {緑地|りょくち} as a formal land-use category.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {緑地|りょくち}を{整備|せいび}する: to develop green space
- {緑地|りょくち}を{保全|ほぜん}する: to conserve green space
- {緑地|りょくち}{公園|こうえん}: green park; parkland
- {緑地|りょくち}{帯|たい}: green belt

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {公園|こうえん}: park — a developed recreational area with facilities; {緑地|りょくち} may be less developed
- {緑|みどり}: greenery — the plants and vegetation themselves, not the land
- {森林|しんりん}: forest — larger natural wooded areas, not typically urban
